title: Unrestricted pro-modularity at the prime two
main_claim: Every continuous, odd, absolutely irreducible r: G_Q -> GL_2(E), E/Q_2 finite and unramified outside finitely many primes, comes from a continuous point of the full varying-weight 2-adic Hecke algebra T_2(N) for some odd N, with T_l -> tr r(Frob_l) and l S_l -> det r(Frob_l). There is no de Rham hypothesis and no residual hypothesis.
coverage:
I read all six sections in full. Results:
(1) Lemma 2.1, the determinant normalization: the square-root construction of beta works, beta(-1)=1 so oddness is kept, and alpha*beta^2=z^w.
(2) Lemma 2.2, the dimension counts: framed component B has dim >= 6 and trace family D has dim >= 3, from h^0((ad^0 r)^vee(1))=0 plus a real local ring of dim 2. The virtually-solvable loci have small dimension (induced from quadratic fields: integral dim <= 2; exceptional finite projective image: <= 1).
(3) Prop 2.3, potential support: the degree and cut inequalities (2d_A-3-u_A-kappa > d_A; 2d-2m-4-u_0 > d) are consistent. The hypotheses match FM2's Thm 5.1 (localized propagation), which explicitly allows the determinant and the residue to be chosen separately.
(4) Section 3, one-factor admissibility: the full-corner lemma; the principal-series K-coinvariant computation (stabilizers have det 1, so the ideals for a-1 and a^{-1}-1 agree); the exclusion of repeated characters on characteristic-2 curves (by injectivity of squaring); and the iterated tensor argument against product admissibility. All hold.
(5) Section 4, regular point: the growth-drop inequality H_{M/fM}(n) <= H_M(n)-H_M(n-c) is correct. The chain gives g(V) >= dim D + 1 >= 4, hence positive rank. This matches the known projectivity numerology for GL2/Q with dim T = 3. The sign character of GL_2(F_2)=S_3 is its unique cuspidal representation, and u-1 is invertible on sigma⊗U, which excludes all reducible Banach simples. Depth-zero supercuspidality then gives tame WD parameters. Every ramified character of Q_2^x is wild because Z_2^x=U^1, so the CM case of Newton–Thorne is excluded.
(6) Section 6, final step: the local counts are h^1_2=5 and H^1_f dim 2 (Bloch–Kato), so the quotient at 2 is 3 and the quotients away from 2 are 0, giving H^1(G_S, ad) <= 3. The regular-local-ring factorization lemma is correct.
(7) Section 5, Hecke continuity and twists: Weierstrass preparation on Theta_X and the finite-order twist step are fine.
I did not re-verify the companion results used as black boxes: FM2 (Thm 1.1, Thm 5.1, Prop 3.6, Prop 4.1/4.2, Lemmas 7.2–7.5) and Dim (Thm 1.1: every component has dim 4; Prop 2.3, Prop 4.1). Neither companion cites this paper, so the dependence is not circular.
sibling_notes: Family 010 board was empty when I started. The argument depends heavily on FM2 'Fontaine–Mazur modularity at the prime 2' (Thm 5.1 localized propagation with determinant and residue chosen separately, Prop 4.2 local-global block comparison, Lemmas 7.3–7.5 connectedness) and on 'The Dimension of the Two-Adic Hecke Algebra at Odd Level' (Thm 1.1: every component of T_2(N) has dim 4). If siblings find a gap in either of those, this paper inherits it.
